title: Initial contact between SARS-CoV-2 spike S1 protein and cell surface glycans involves multiple binding modes
authors: Michela Parafioriti; Minghong Ni; Maurice Petitou; Courtney J. Mycroft-West; Timothy R. Rudd; Neha S. Gandhi; Vito Ferro; Jeremy E. Turnbull; Marcelo A. Lima; Mark A. Skidmore; David G. Fernig; Edwin A. Yates; Antonella Bisio; Marco Guerrini; Stefano Elli
one_liner_zh: 该文通过NMR和分子动力学模拟研究SARS-CoV-2刺突蛋白S1与肝素糖的多种低特异性结合模式，虽非TF-DNA体系，但属于蛋白质-糖类互作且MD方法可迁移至蛋白-DNA界面建模，对课题有间接启发。
abstract: Infection of host cells by SARS-CoV-2 begins with recognition by the virus S (spike) protein of cell surface heparan sulfate (HS), tethering the virus to the extracellular matrix environment, and causing the subunit S1-RBD to undergo a conformational change into the ‘open’ conformation. These two events promote the binding of S1-RBD to the angiotensin converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor, a preliminary step toward viral-cell membrane fusion. Combining ligand-based NMR spectroscopy with molecular dynamics, oligosaccharide analogues were used to explore the interactions between S1-RBD of SARS CoV-2 and HS, revealing several low-specificity binding modes and previously unidentified potential sites for the binding of extended HS polysaccharide chains. The evident multiplicity of binding modes also suggests that highly specific inhibitors will not be optimal against protein S but, rather, diverse HS-based structures, characterized by high affinity and including multi-valent compounds, may be required
abstract_zh: SARS-CoV-2对宿主细胞的感染始于病毒S（刺突）蛋白对细胞表面硫酸乙酰肝素（HS）的识别，将病毒锚定于细胞外基质环境，并促使亚基S1-RBD发生构象变化进入“开放”构象。这两个事件促进S1-RBD与血管紧张素转换酶2（ACE2）受体的结合，这是病毒-细胞膜融合的初步步骤。结合基于配体的核磁共振波谱（NMR）与分子动力学，利用寡糖类似物探索了SARS-CoV-2的S1-RBD与HS之间的相互作用，揭示了多种低特异性结合模式以及先前未识别的延伸HS多糖链潜在结合位点。结合模式的明显多样性也表明，高度特异性抑制剂并非针对蛋白S的最佳选择，相反，可能需要以高亲和力为特征、包含多价化合物的多样化HS基结构。
